title: Component matching and special centres for regular trait curve models
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $T_1,T_2\to S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $T_i$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], nodal geometric curve fibres and smooth generic fibres. Fix a $K$-isomorphism $\alpha:(T_1)_K\cong(T_2)_K$. Then each $T_i$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed integral regular surfaces of dimension two [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Every such component dominates $S$, its generic fibre is nonempty integral and dense, and taking generic fibres gives a bijection between these components and the irreducible components of $(T_i)_K$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Thus $\alpha$ uniquely matches the components and gives an isomorphism of dense generic open subschemes for each matched pair. For every matched pair there exists a regular integral common $S$-scheme $V$ with two morphisms to the pair inducing this prescribed generic isomorphism, each a finite composition of blowups of reduced closed points [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Every centre of either sequence is in the special fibre. More generally every closed point at every stage of any finite reduced-closed-point blowup sequence over either $T_i$ maps to the closed point of $S$, so every such sequence is unchanged generically. Taking the finite disjoint union of these componentwise comparisons gives a comparison of $T_1,T_2$. No connectedness or geometric integrality of their generic fibres is required. Here nodal geometric curve fibres are nonempty reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one whose nonsmooth closed points over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; they may be disconnected [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Agent componentwise trait refinement of Tag 0C5S (lemma-birational-regular-surfaces): old common-model step 2, including flatness excluding vertical components and properness forcing special centres.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], every nonzero $r\in R$ is a unit times a power of $\pi$. Consequently $K=R[1/\pi]$, and a nonzero prime of $R$ contains $\pi$, so $S$ has precisely the generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}K=D(\pi)\hookrightarrow S$ is an open immersion; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $(T_i)_K$ is the corresponding open subscheme of $T_i$. Also $R$ is Noetherian because all its ideals are principal [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; thus $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and is quasi-compact since it has only two points. Each $T_i\to S$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper].

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; schemes.tex Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); morphisms.tex Tag 01WC.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] to each $T_i/S$: flatness, finite presentation, smooth generic fibre and the explicitly defined nodal geometric fibres are exactly its hypotheses. It gives that $T_i$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-regularization] to $T_i/S$. Every arrow in its sequence must blow up a point at which the preceding total scheme is not regular. Since $T_i$ is regular, a first arrow is impossible; hence the sequence has length zero. Its terminal decomposition therefore says that $T_i$ itself is a finite disjoint union of integral regular surfaces of dimension two. In a disjoint-union decomposition each summand is open and closed; equivalently its complement is the union of the other open summands. Denote these summands by $C_{ia}$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), clause (1) and the length-zero case; dimension/component refinement already stated by lem-sfb-nodal-trait-regularization.

proof.text: For any $C=C_{ia}$ choose a point $x$. If its image is $\eta$, then $C_K$ is nonempty. If its image is $s$, the local map $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}\to A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism] (the local ring is unchanged on an open summand). Its maximal ideal lies over $(\pi)$. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to $(0)\subset(\pi)$ and this maximal ideal: a prime of $A$ lies over $(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], primes of $A$ are primes contained in the prime of $x$ in any affine neighbourhood, so this prime gives a generalization of $x$ in $C_K$. Thus $C_K$ is nonempty in both cases. It is an open subscheme of the integral scheme $C$, hence integral: its nonempty affine opens have domain rings, and it is nonempty [def-pc-integral-scheme]. It is dense since a nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense. In particular $C$ dominates $S$.

source.place: Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), stalk/localization interpretation; properties.tex Tags 01OK, 01ON.

proof.text: The opens $C_{ia,K}$ partition $(T_i)_K$ into finitely many nonempty closed and open integral subschemes. An irreducible subset can meet only one of these summands: intersections with a summand and its complement would disconnect it. Each summand is itself irreducible and closed, so they are exactly the maximal irreducible closed subsets, namely the irreducible components. This proves the generic-fibre bijection. The isomorphism $\alpha$ carries maximal irreducible closed subsets bijectively to maximal irreducible closed subsets, and therefore determines a unique matching $a\leftrightarrow b$ with $\alpha(C_{1a,K})=C_{2b,K}$. Its restriction is an isomorphism of these dense open subschemes. The induced open structures agree because these are open subschemes of the generic fibres.

source.place: Agent component bookkeeping preceding the application of Tag 0C5S; elementary finite disjoint-union argument.

proof.text: For a matched pair $C_1,C_2$, their closed immersions into the proper schemes $T_1,T_2$ make them proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Step 2 gives integrality, regularity and dimension two, Step 1 gives that $S$ is Noetherian, and Steps 3--4 give the prescribed $S$-isomorphism between dense generic open subschemes. These are all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-common-regular-surface-resolution]. Obtain a regular integral common $S$-scheme $V$ and morphisms $q_j:V\to C_j$, each a finite tower of reduced-closed-point blowups inducing that prescribed birational identification. No geometric integrality or connectedness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 0C5S (lemma-birational-regular-surfaces), with the specified rational map; morphisms.tex Tag 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper).

proof.text: Consider any reduced-closed-point blowup tower $Z_r\to\cdots\to Z_0$, where $Z_0$ is either $T_i$ or one of its summands. Initially $Z_0\to S$ is proper by Steps 1 and 5, hence $Z_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $S$ is Noetherian and proper morphisms are finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Inductively, the ideal of a reduced closed point on a Noetherian scheme is of finite type (on a Noetherian affine neighbourhood it is an ideal in a Noetherian ring). Its blowup is proper by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], and the next structure map is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. The same finite-type-over-Noetherian statement makes the next scheme Noetherian, completing the induction. At any stage a closed singleton has closed image in $S$, since its structure map is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This nonempty singleton image cannot be $\{\eta\}$, which is not closed; it is $\{s\}$. Thus every closed point of every stage, and in particular every centre, is special.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); properness as recorded by thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper; morphisms.tex Tags 01T6, 01W1, 01W3.

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], each arrow of any tower in Step 6 is an isomorphism off its centre. Since the centre is special, its restriction on generic fibres is an isomorphism. Composing proves the generic invariance for arbitrary finite towers, including the empty tower, and for both towers supplied in Step 5. In particular $q_{j,K}$ are isomorphisms. To check that $q_{2,K}=\alpha\circ q_{1,K}$ on the whole generic fibre, the prescribed birational identification gives agreement on a dense open of $V$. Intersect it with the nonempty open $V_K$; the intersection is nonempty and dense in the integral scheme $V_K$. This intersection is schematically dense: on each nonempty affine domain chart, a section zero on a nonempty principal open is killed by a nonzero element, so is zero. The target $C_2$ is separated over $S$ by properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] extends the equality from that dense open to all of $V_K$.

source.place: Tag 0C5S, specified birational map; divisors.tex Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), clause (1); separated uniqueness as in the cited blueprint lemma.

proof.text: Finally take $W=\coprod_a V_a$ over the finitely many matched pairs. The two families of composites $V_a\to C_{ia}\hookrightarrow T_i$ give morphisms $W\to T_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Their generic restrictions are the componentwise isomorphisms of Step 7, with compatibility $q_{2,K}=\alpha\circ q_{1,K}$ on each open summand; these equations give the same compatibility globally by the coproduct mapping property. This is the required comparison. The matching used only ordinary integral generic fibres, and did not require them to remain integral over an algebraic closure or require either whole generic fibre to be connected.
